newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Waigel says ERM link, then euro for Sweden - paper.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says ERM link, then euro for Sweden - paper.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said Sweden must be a member of Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) in order to join the euro, but Sweden disagrees, Swedish daily Dagens Nyheter reported on Tuesday.
"On that point the Maastricht treaty is unambiguous. It applies to all countries, including Sweden," Waigel told the newspaper.
But Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink repeated to Dagens Nyheter that he disagreed with this point of view.
"That's the way Germany and several other countries think. But we have another point of view," the newspaper quoted Asbrink as saying.
Waigel has said any country wishing to join a single currency must be an ERM member. Sweden argues currency stability is the key issue, not necessarily participation in ERM.
Asbrink said last week that it would take a few more weeks before his minority Social Democratic government would present its views on EMU membership.

The government has previously said it would voice its opinion by the end of May. A party congress will then vote about a possible link in September and a parliamentary ruling will follow before the end of the year.
